text:
Maya (AE): Urgent - demo POC failing with 413 when they inline images as base64 in the chat history. They want one-shot request for the deck walkthrough. Body ~140KB. Endpoint: POST /v1/generate model=rw-chat-8k. Any fast options?
Omar (SE): Can you paste the raw gateway error?
Maya (AE): They forwarded this from their logs:
ingest-bot: gateway: client 172.16.4.2 rejected request: request_entity_too_large, length=142560, client_max_body_size=104857
Priya (SRE): That's our front proxy cap (~100KB). It blocks the request before runtime. Inlining base64 can bloat payload ~30%+ vs binary.
Omar (SE): Short-term mitigations (no infra changes):
- Compress JSON: gzip and set Content-Encoding: gzip (we accept this)
- Offload attachments: presigned object upload, then pass a short context_url or object id
- Send only last N turns and a brief summarized blob of earlier conversation
- Chunked append: multiple small requests to /v1/session/append + final /v1/generate (needs session API support)
Maya (AE): Customer insists on single JSON for demo — can we make an exception?
Priya (SRE): We can't change proxy per-account on hosted without deployment work. Options: temporary Dedicated sandbox with relaxed proxy, or engineering builds chunked-append endpoint (multi-week).
Maya (AE): They also asked if switching to a 32k context model avoids this.
Omar (SE): Bigger context model only helps after the HTTP layer accepts the payload. It doesn't change the HTTP size limit.
DevHelper: Quick gzip example to send the customer:
```
echo -n '{"model":"rw-chat-8k","input":"<LONG_CHAT_WITH_BASE64>"}' | gzip -c | \
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
    -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data-binary @-
```
Omar (SE): Presigned flow sketch to recommend:
1) POST /v1/uploads/initiate -> returns upload_id + presigned PUT URL
2) Client PUTs binary blob to presigned URL (S3)
3) POST /v1/generate {"model":"...","context_url":"s3://bucket/key","upload_id":"..."}
Maya (AE): If they want a single-call sandbox for an in-person demo, can we offer a time-limited environment?
Priya (SRE): Yes — Ops can spin a short-lived dedicated sandbox but it involves costs. Sales should route through pricing for a trial credit offer.
Omar (SE): I'll draft a one-paragraph playbook for AE: 1) try gzip first 2) if not possible, use presigned upload 3) escalate to sandbox request for single-call demo (include cost note).
ingest-bot: ticket INF-960 created: investigate frequent 413s from hosted front proxy and add runbook entry
Maya (AE): Customer tried gzip and it passed through (200). They're checking whether base64 decoding/parsing preserved attachments correctly. Thanks team. :tada:
